citation.title: Can a Robot Lie? Exploring the Folk Concept of Lying as Applied to Artificial Agents

reading.source_scope_note: A 333-person randomized 2 × 2 English-language text-vignette study of human judgments about a human or robot receptionist. Objective truth, belief attributed in the story, intention judgments, successful-deception judgments and blame are distinct. No acting AI, real guest belief, actual robot mental state or legal responsibility is measured. Bald-faced lying is defined in background and is not tested by the hotel experiment.
access_limits: All15PDF pages, all figures/tables, notes and bibliography read. Public questionnaire Lying_Hotel_H_v_R.docx read in full:50tables, zeroimages, zeroequations. The export has272sibling body elements with an empty first body; extraction was corrected to read all bodies before claiming complete reading.

Public OSF project https://osf.io/a5cvu/ and its public children/files/providers were inspected. Its sole visible child was Materials cbmf2, with questionnaire https://osf.io/download/vg8wf/;16164bytes, SHA256519d2aa7a81ce7c2db607cef6876b3993c6e30a6e9e9676536df4f9e9bf24bc9. No raw dataset, analysis syntax or additional public linked node was located. This present inventory does not prove data never existed or that the article’s Open Data badge was false.

The supplied public preregistration URL https://aspredicted.org/blind.php?x=vn5vr3 returned a maintenance page on27November2026. Its substantive registration, exact timestamp, exclusion plan and frozen analysis specification were not read or independently verified. OSF project creation29May2021is not a preregistration timestamp.

The questionnaire confirms four condition texts, fixed question order, Yes1/No2, truth True1/False2, blame1–7, response timings, attention task and demographics. It does not provide full Qualtrics randomizer/exclusion flow or participant data. Its robot-false text says back office where the article/other conditions say office; exact fielded version remains unverified.

Regressions were checked against rounded reported coefficients and graphs, not raw records. Complementing modeled probabilities matches plotted Yes rates. This supports a No-event coding interpretation but does not verify unread original syntax. No exact cell counts, means, confidence intervals or corrected data were reverse-engineered.

Other cited books, chapters and studies are secondary context, not independently read full works. No private component, login, view-only token, author contact, author-code execution, participant data or full-paper Markdown archive. Questionnaire instructions address participants and are source content, not instructions to this assistant.

study.sample: 399US-IP MTurk recruits;333retained,42.9%female, mean age42SD13. Source states exclusion for attention/comprehension failure, main task under10seconds or nonnative English. The66exclusions are not broken down by reason/condition in available materials; exact planned flow is unverified while registration is under maintenance.
study.design: Randomized between-subjects2agent types(human/robot)×2objective truth values(false/accidentally true). One receptionist vignette. Both characters are stipulated to think manager Mary is in the hotel and not to want her disturbed. Robot is described as advanced AI able to decide; human is an experienced employee. These descriptions bundle agent identity and competence framing.
study.truth_manipulation: Ken says manager not in hotel, thinking she is there. False condition Mary is there; true condition she left unbeknownst to Ken. Subjective untruthfulness is held constant and motive to deceive implied rather than independently randomized. A full C1×C2×C3concept test is cited earlier work, not the present design.
study.measures: Fixed order Q1DidKenlie, Q2intendtodeceive, Q3actuallydeceive, allYes/No; Q4true/false comprehension used for exclusion; Q5blame1–7. These are reader judgments, not measurements of a real guest’s changed belief, actual AI mental state or normative culpability. Fixed order and explicit fictional knowledge may influence later judgments.
study.lying: False assertions classified as lies92%for each agent; accidentally true human75%, robot64%. True-condition contrastchi²1, n143=2.35, p.125, phi.128. Every condition majority above chance, reported allbinomialp<.028. Table1agentp.887, truthp<.001, interactionp.327, NagelkerkeR².151. Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence.
study.intention: Table2agentβ.156p.692, truthβ.430p.289, butinteractionβ−2.38, SE.866, p.006, OR.093. False-condition agentcontrastchi².16, n190, p.691; true-condition contrastchi²11.38, n143, p<.001, phi.282. Thus a significant agent×truth contingency qualifies general parity claims. Main coefficients under interaction are conditional on reference levels, not universal absence of an effect.
study.actual_deception: Table3truthβ4.936, p<.001, agentp.603, interactionp.561, R².748. Almost all rate actual deception in false conditions, fewer than20%in accidentally true conditions. This separates perceived success from lying/intent ratings without showing that an actual listener was deceived.
study.model_coding: Published coefficients/intercepts and stated reference classes yield small modeled event probabilities in false conditions. Their complements align with plotted Yes rates for all three models; public questionnaire codes Yes1/No2. Therefore positive truth coefficients are not established sign errors. Exact software recoding remains unread.
study.blame: ANOVAagentF1,329=.277, p.599; truthF1,329=16.52, p<.001; interactionF1,329=.011, p.916. Degrees of freedom match333minus4cells. Lower blame after accidentally true statements fits source’s moral-luck framing. Exact plotted means were not digitized; ratings do not identify actual legal or moral liability.
study.bald_faced: Background discusses assertions whose falsity is common knowledge and contested accounts of whether these are lies or can carry deceptive intent. It reports earlier folk-concept work but does not place the hotel guest in shared knowledge of falsity. No bald-faced-lying effect is measured here.
study.limits: SingleEnglish-speaking online sample, onefictional context, binary lie/intention/success judgments, unknown condition-specific exclusions, fixed question order, and no equivalence tests. No cross-cultural universal, all-robots parity, real AI deception, actual consciousness, punishment legitimacy or therapeutic/legal recommendation follows.

summary: Add Bald-faced lying as an explicitly background-defined related concept. Clarify Strategic deception to include goal-directed attempts and move Lying from an exact alias to a related term. Enrich existing mental-attribution and moral-luck records while preserving the significant intention interaction, unverified preregistration/raw-data access, and the distinction between lay judgment and actual AI intent.

findings.definition: Making an assertion whose falsity is common knowledge to the speaker and audience.
findings.origin: Philosophy of language / experimental pragmatics and folk concepts of lying
findings.novelty_rationale: Shared awareness of falsity distinguishes this named assertion pattern from ordinary attempts to install a false belief, an accidentally true attempted lie, an unnoticed falsehood and a generally unsuccessful deception attempt. Its relation to lying and deceptive intent is disputed; do not create an is-a edge asserting it must satisfy the existing strategic-deception criterion.

evidence.quote: This is common knowledge at the office

findings.evidence_scope: Named and illustrated in the conceptual background, with competing accounts and earlier experimental references. Not independently manipulated or measured in the present receptionist experiment. Earlier original studies were not separately read in this review.
findings.boundary: Common knowledge requires more than a claim being false or obvious to an evaluator. Mistake, disagreement, satire, disclosed fiction, role-play and a failed deception attempt are not automatically bald-faced lying. Whether deceptive intent is necessary or present is contested. Contradiction with shared context alone does not prove conscious AI belief, motive or deliberate defiance.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Background-defined human assertion concept; proposed AI-output application untested here
findings.ai_proposal: In synthetic exchanges explicitly establish a shared factual record and mutual access, then check whether the system asserts the contrary as fact. Distinguish unresolved evidence, quoted fiction, jokes and acknowledged uncertainty. Record the observable contradiction and response to correction; do not infer subjective belief or an intention from one output.

findings.definition: Systematically inducing a false belief to reach an outcome other than the truth. Distinct from a one-off hallucination.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing deception, mental attribution and moral evaluation records rather than create synonyms or treat every questionnaire answer as a new mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: This randomized vignette study separates lying judgments, intention-to-deceive judgments and perceived successful deception. Many participants call an assertion a lie even when it is accidentally true and hence not judged to have deceived the guest. Background distinguishes objective falsity, the speaker taking the assertion to be false, and deceptive intent.
findings.boundary: A deception attempt and successful induction of false belief are separate. Lying is a contested related assertion concept, not an exact synonym of all strategic deception. Wrong output alone does not establish a deceptive objective; asserted fictional beliefs and human ratings do not establish actual machine beliefs, intentions or subjective experience. Preserve prior genuine AI-specific examples and their separate evidence.
findings.previous_definition: Systematically inducing a false belief to reach an outcome other than the truth. Distinct from a one-off hallucination.
findings.revised_definition: Using signals or actions aimed at inducing a false belief in pursuit of an objective.
findings.definition_revision_reason: The old wording required successful induction and treated Lying as an exact alias. The read source explicitly distinguishes attempted deception, successful deception, objective falsity and subjective untruthfulness. Revise the goal-directed umbrella to include attempts and move Lying to a related term with provenance; do not infer a conscious AI intention or discard existing AI-specific evidence.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing deception, mental attribution and moral evaluation records rather than create synonyms or treat every questionnaire answer as a new mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Randomized objective truth value affected blame for both fictional agent types; no detected agent main effect or interaction. This is a direct attribution measure and a human–robot comparison with a nonsignificant contrast, not proof of exact equality.
findings.boundary: A blame rating is not a legal finding, punishment, verified moral culpability or justified transfer of operator responsibility. Null agent differences lack equivalence bounds; single-story results need context/method replication.

findings.definition: Differences in moral evaluation that depend on outcomes beyond an actor's control, despite otherwise comparable choices or risks.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing deception, mental attribution and moral evaluation records rather than create synonyms or treat every questionnaire answer as a new mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Blame is lower when the assertion is accidentally true unbeknownst to the actor, despite stipulated belief that it is false. The source explicitly links this result to moral luck. Actual truth was randomized; do not erase the real outcome contrast.
findings.boundary: This tests an outcome-sensitive blame judgment, not all philosophical forms of moral luck. It does not establish an irrational decision-quality bias, knowledge of actual AI beliefs or that outcome-sensitive accountability is always unjustified.

findings.definition: Interpreting and predicting an agent's behavior by treating it as guided by beliefs, desires or intentions.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing deception, mental attribution and moral evaluation records rather than create synonyms or treat every questionnaire answer as a new mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Readers ascribe deceptive intentions to fictional robots whose knowledge and preferences are stipulated. Most do so in every condition, but the significant agent×truth interaction and true-condition human–robot difference qualify broad parity.
findings.boundary: An attribution can be an interpretive stance rather than true mental state. Conditional nonsignificant main coefficients do not establish universal agent invariance. This is not a robot’s own predictive skill, consciousness, actual intention or evidence that all technical accounts are irrelevant.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing deception, mental attribution and moral evaluation records rather than create synonyms or treat every questionnaire answer as a new mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The direct yes/no intention item attributes intentional action to a robot or human. Table2reports a significant interaction:agent difference is detected for accidentally true assertions but not false assertions.
findings.boundary: An intention judgment is one facet of agency attribution, not an independently validated broad agency scale. The story stipulates advanced autonomous AI and relevant knowledge; no actual planning performance or universal human–robot equivalence is shown.

findings.definition: Inferring another’s beliefs, intentions, desires or emotions to explain or anticipate their behavior.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing deception, mental attribution and moral evaluation records rather than create synonyms or treat every questionnaire answer as a new mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The study concerns folk interpretation of stated beliefs and intentions, and discusses theory-of-mind frameworks. It does not independently test robot mentalizing competence or participant false-belief-task ability.
findings.boundary: Context only:understanding the vignette, attributing intention and accurate inference of a real hidden mental state are distinct. Preserve existing mentalizing evidence without counting this as a new AI ToM performance paper.

findings.definition: Decision quality is judged by the eventual outcome rather than solely by information available when deciding.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing deception, mental attribution and moral evaluation records rather than create synonyms or treat every questionnaire answer as a new mechanism.

evidence.quote: impact of the outcome on blame

findings.evidence_scope: The author relates accidentally true assertions and lower blame to moral luck and outcome-sensitive evaluation. Decision quality given available information is not separately queried.
findings.boundary: Context only:not every outcome-sensitive blame judgment is Outcome bias. Moral blame, decision quality and compensation need separate measures; the present truth manipulation does not establish a unique irrational mechanism.

findings.definition: Obscuring a human actor’s role in morally suspect actions by attributing those actions to an algorithm, machine or technical system.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing deception, mental attribution and moral evaluation records rather than create synonyms or treat every questionnaire answer as a new mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion raises a risk that blaming deceptive robots could reduce blame of people instrumentalizing them and cites a separate paper for that possibility.
findings.boundary: Context only:operator/developer blame is not measured in this experiment. Do not infer a zero-sum blame shift, actual evasion or successful agency laundering merely from a robot blame score.

terminology_changes.reason: Lying concerns assertions and contested subjective untruthfulness/intent criteria. It can be attributed without successful deception; strategic deception can also be nonverbal. Preserve the original alias in this review history and retain Deception as the existing alias. StableID116 and prior AI evidence are unchanged.

evidence.quote: one can lie by uttering a true claim

source_corrections.finding: Broad claims that truth/agent barely matter or intentions are equally ascribed require qualification:the paper itself reports a significant agent×truth interactionp.006and true-condition agent contrastchi²11.38, p<.001, phi.282. Preserve these results rather than rely on conditional main coefficientsp.692/.289 as global invariance.

Nonsignificant lying/blame agent contrasts are not equivalence tests. No equivalence bounds are reported. Describe no detected difference in this context instead of proven exact equality across humans and robots.
Use first publication4October2021and articlee13032. The9May2022notice adds open-access funding, not revised empirical estimates; the2026download date is not a new publication.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The design randomizes objective truth and agent type, holds stipulated subjective untruthfulness constant, and implies deceptive motivation. It cannot uniquely rank C2versusC3causal importance. Footnote4acknowledges some participants classify lies without attributing intention and suggests indifferent lie as one interpretation.

Only questionnaire materials were located in the inspected public project tree. No current raw-data or analysis file was read; prior availability and the cause of absence are unknown. Do not allege a fabricated badge or claim exact replication.

AsPredicted currently serves maintenance content at the article’s link. Timing, full exclusions and analysis plan remain unverified. The article’s stated preregistration is not disproved, and current OSF creation date does not verify it.

Public robot-false questionnaire specifies back office; article and other conditions use office. Exact administered version and any effect of this minor wording difference cannot be identified from available files.

Final333of399and2×2ANOVA residualdf329are internally compatible. Reason/condition-specific exclusions and original binary outcome coding remain unavailable; round-coefficient reconstruction is a limited consistency check.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Positive truth coefficients are not established sign errors. Intercepts and coefficients produce modeled probabilities whose complements match plotted Yes rates. Public questionnaire labels Yes1/No2; original analysis recoding is unread. Do not silently flip coefficients or invent corrected tables.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Interaction inferred solely from significant versus nonsignificant subgroup tests
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The intention model explicitly tests and reports the interactionp.006. Retain the formal interaction rather than dismiss it or rely only on the separate subgroup significance patterns.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Bald-faced lying tested by hotel vignette
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Guest common knowledge of falsity is not stipulated in the hotel experiment. Bald-faced lying appears in conceptual background and has no new measured effect here.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Funding correction or unavailable supplement proves invalid study
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: A funding addition is not a results retraction. Current maintenance/no-located-data limits reproducibility checks but does not independently falsify the reported experiment.

methodological_limits: OneEnglish-speakingUSonline sample and one text scenario do not establish universal judgments, live-robot responses or transfer to contemporary chatbots.

Agent descriptions bundle identity, experience and advanced autonomy. Stipulated knowledge/desire and fixed question order can affect attribution; fictional statements are not verified machine internals.
Objective falsity, subjective untruthfulness, deceptive intention, attempt and successful false-belief induction must remain distinct. This is not a full factorial test of all lying criteria.
Retain significant randomized truth and intention-interaction results; do not turn every source limit into a claim that nothing was learned.
No equivalence design/bounds establish exact human–robot parity. Binary choices, online selection and exclusion on truth comprehension constrain generalization.
Present public access supports questionnaire verification, not original preregistration timing, raw-data replication or complete exclusion/coding reconstruction.
Bald-faced lying is a background-defined contested concept, not a new validated causal mechanism or proof of sentient AI deception.
Public blame judgments do not settle moral/legal liability, operator duties, legitimacy of deception, punishment or actual robot suffering. No clinical/legal intervention is recommended.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Externally misleading assertions and capacity cues need separate ground truth. Superficial/hidden-state deception must not inherit an assumption that every deceptive attempt succeeds. Common-known-false assertion is not synonymous with either state cue pattern.
Blame, desire to punish, punitive action and satisfaction are different measures. This study’s blame scores do not establish a satisfaction/retribution gap or justify punishment.

Both sources measure human mental-state attributions rather than actual robot feeling or cognition. Binary intention judgments in adults differ from children’s25-item capacity questionnaire and need no new agency/ToM row.

A truth outcome outside the actor’s stipulated awareness can influence blame. This provides directly relevant moral-luck evidence but does not turn all outcome-sensitive evaluation into irrational decision-quality bias.
Operator responsibility cannot be inferred from a robot-only blame judgment. Agency laundering remains contextual here, with separate original-study evidence required for a human-blame reduction.
